home.heading: Home
home.presentation: I'm a frontend developer that enjoys crafting intuitive and efficient user interfaces. Always exploring new technologies, I focus on creating seamless digital experiences.

about.heading: About Me
about.paragraph1: My background might not be the most traditional for a developer. I have nine years of experience working in schools and preschools, including over three years as a preschool teacher. During that time, I learned how to communicate effectively, collaborate closely, and adapt quickly to new situations. I’ve carried those skills with me into development, where problem-solving, creativity, and teamwork are just as important as writing code.
about.paragraph2: Coding means a lot to me, because it allows me to think deeply, build things from nothing, and constantly learn. I code almost every day and enjoy working in environments where I can both collaborate and take initiative. I see feedback as a natural part of growing, and I’m always striving to improve my skills.
about.paragraph3: I'm really looking forward to the opportunity to contribute with my energy and skills.

projects.heading: My Portfolio
projects.no-projects: No projects available at this moment.

3D-Print-&-Konsult.description:
3D Print Konsult is a 3D printing business run by Vadim Artemenkov, a skilled and passionate individual who offers professional 3D printing services. Vadim reached out to me to help modernize and continue developing his website.

When I started working on this project, I had very little experience with WordPress, but it quickly turned into an excellent learning opportunity. Since then, I've refined the site's design, implemented custom CSS, and improved its overall performance and usability.

It's been a fun and rewarding project that has taught me a lot about web development and WordPress. I continue to enhance the website and explore new ways to optimize it further. Feel free to check out the website through the link below or contact Vadim directly if you're interested in his 3D printing services.

React-Oddball-Icons.description: A playful React icon library featuring quirky corporate-style icons. It’s fully typed for TypeScript and easy to install and use. You can also check out the library’s official website, built with React and Tailwind, for a full preview of all the icons.

TinySaves.description: A savings goal application designed for users who are new to saving, encouraging small, regular contributions. You can save in different currencies, customize your profile, earn milestone awards, and track your full saving history on a statistics page.

Drinkory.description: A website for anyone who loves drinks. You can look up drinks, learn how to make them step by step, and save your favorites. You can also search by alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks, or roll the dice to get a random suggestion if you're in the mood for something new.

Tic-Tac-Toe.description: This is a Tic-tac-toe game I built as a school project, and also my first project with Vue. The game is simple: Just enter each player’s name and just press play to begin. you can challenge a friend to see who scores the most points.

PokeSearch.description: A nerdy little game that tests your knowledge of classic Pokémon. The premise is simple: type as many of the original 151 Pokémon as you can within a time limit to put your knowledge to the test. It was also my very first project built entirely with vanilla JavaScript.

To-Do.description: Just a simple To-do list I made with vanilla JavaScript. You can mark tasks as done and even sort them by completed or pending.

TheZoo.description: My last individual school project in React. A fictional zoo website with different animals that need to be fed every couple of hours. Each animal has its own bio with information about its respective species.

EmployeeSite.description: A code test made in Vue for an internship application. It is a fictional employee site that showcases a list of employees for the company. The site uses mock API data.

ariaAI.title: Aria AI
ariaAI.description:
My latest feature for Are You Coming? is Aria AI, an AI assistant built to help users understand and navigate the application.

I am also working on another AI feature that will suggest titles and descriptions for planned events based on context.

This is my first real dive into AI integration and it has been very productive so far.

areYouComing.title: Are You Coming?
areYouComing.description:
A simple event planning app where you can create events, share them with friends, and let them RSVP, no account required for guests.

It comes with a live countdown, an attendee list with email reminders, a calendar view, and a Spotify playlist embed to set the vibe for your event.

Built with Next.js App Router, TypeScript, PostgreSQL via Neon, NextAuth v5 for Google sign-in, and Tailwind CSS. More features to come!

welcome.title: Welcome!
welcome.description: This page is dedicated to giving updates on my current work. Here, I will give you a look at what I'm currently building, learning, or experimenting with.

skill-descriptions.stack: I work with JavaScript and TypeScript, using frameworks like Vue.js and Next.js to build web applications. I’m familiar with styling tools like Tailwind CSS and Sass and have experience with databases like MongoDB and MySQL. I have also used tools like Postman, Jest, and Figma to support development and testing.
skill-descriptions.languages: I can confidently communicate in Swedish, Spanish, and English, both spoken and written, adapting my language to suit professional and social settings.
